questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before riding. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Which clothing choice is NOT good for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles

questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, not a baseball cap. Also wear face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When it rains, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when it rains. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for the safest grip.

questions.question: Which fabric offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants give the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When choosing where to ride in a lane, you should think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in a certain position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. Keep enough space around your motorcycle to stay safe.

questions.question: Common over-the-counter drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
Usually won't affect your riding ability.
Pose no risk to your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can make you cross into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make you cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Going too fast around a corner can make you cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Has been in a previous crash.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. A helmet should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because riders and other drivers often conflict there.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It takes only a few minutes and helps keep you safe.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots. What should you do about them?

options.text: They do not have blind spots because they are small.
They have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
They are too small to have blind spots.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire traction. These include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. Dry pavement is not slippery for motorcycles.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle you have never used before, what should you do?

options.text: Check if the seat is comfortable.
Assume it is in good condition.
Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride normally since most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different, so be careful with an unfamiliar one. Learn how it works before you ride it. Practice the gear pattern by using the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, what should you do?

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of the lane.
Always stay on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is normal and not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight at a steady speed. Trying to angle your ride to stop the weave is dangerous because it will make you zigzag in your lane.

questions.question: What happens if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is safe as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could end up in another lane or off the road. Always use caution when turning.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and hope to wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take rest breaks at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when braking and avoid making sudden movements.
